text:
Two players carry this one. Connor Hellebuyck, our projected starter for New Jersey, has spent the week in the headlines after his first trip back to Winnipeg: Yahoo News Canada's headline said death threats motivated his trade request out of Canada, and the Devils sat him for that game. In Devils colors he's at .916 and 1.9 goals saved above expected over six games. At the other end is Alex Ovechkin, in what TSN called his final season and without a goal in twelve games on 3.9 expected goals (the quality of his chances). That is a drought the chances say shouldn't last, but it has lasted.

This is the back half of a home-and-home. The Devils won Thursday 5-2 in what the chances called a coin flip, and they are second in the Metropolitan, eight points clear of fourth-place Washington. New Jersey is better than its record suggests: 58% of the expected goals at five on five, with goaltending costing it 5.4 goals. Jack Hughes (six goals, seven assists) and Jesper Bratt (two and seven) both bring seven-game point streaks, and Bratt has 10 points in six games against Washington. The Devils are short on the back end, though, with Brett Pesce, Vladislav Kolyachonok and Johnathan Kovacevic out and Anton Silaev called up from Utica.

The Capitals are 2-3-0 in their last five and have been outscored 21-15. Charlie Lindgren is in line to start over Logan Thompson, who has 12 of 17 starts; Lindgren is at -0.7 goals saved above expected. Our playoff model has New Jersey at 95% and Washington at 55%.

Both of our sleepers are Devils. Arseny Gritsyuk, a third-liner at about 16:10 a night, has 2.6 expected goals in his last 10 games, better than 80% of depth forwards; we have him at 23% to score and 50% for a point. Luke Evangelista, one goal from 50 in his career, is at 54% for a point against a season pace of 47%, because his line creates 4.09 expected goals per 60 and the Capitals allow the 9th-most.
headline: Hellebuyck, Ovechkin and the end of a home-and-home
